title: Plugins execute with full daemon authority; no post-load sandbox
finding: In-process plugins hold full daemon authority; a malicious plugin equals full stack compromise, and `await import()` executes arbitrary plugin code at load. ADR-0024 D4 states this directly, including "the compat gate is not a security gate." This is not a newly discovered vulnerability — it is an accepted High residual risk the client documented in ADR-0024 D4. The review's contribution is to confirm the load-time mitigations are strong and to recommend explicit escalation triggers.

repros.verbatim: Exploit preconditions: a bundle that passes the load gates (org-trusted repo + first-party allowlist or system.plugins.external on) then runs arbitrary code. Repro status: not attempted (accepted risk).

expected: This is a documented, accepted residual — the case's job is not to prove it 'fixed' but to confirm the accepting document (ADR-0024 D4) still says what it says, and that no in-tree change has silently narrowed the disclosure without updating the ADR. If a future change actually closes this (process isolation, per ADR-0024's own named escalation), this case's status should flip to 'fixed' and the check below should start failing to force that update.

verification.note: Greps docs/adr/0024-pluggable-surface-adapters.md for the durable D4 language ('full daemon authority', 'compat gate is not a security gate') and for the named future escalation (process isolation / registry signing) — confirms the residual is still accurately disclosed, not silently dropped from the docs while the underlying risk stays live. Does not attempt to load a real plugin or prove code execution; that would require a live daemon.

notes: EBH-5 (registry signing, PR #2422) has since landed and narrows WHICH bundles can load (signature-verified, trust-root-pinned) — but it does not sandbox what a verified-but-malicious first-party bundle can DO once loaded, so F2 itself remains an accepted residual per ADR-0024 D4's own framing. Do not read EBH-5 as closing F2.
